title: Chapter 55
text: Sources A large number of the poems published in the posthumous collections, especially beginning with What Matters Most Is How Well You Walk Through the Fire (1999), differ—sometimes radically so—from the manuscript version of the very same poems. In an attempt to rescue Bukowski’s genuine voice and style, the poems in this volume are faithful reproductions of the original manuscripts. If a given manuscript could not be found, then the appropriate magazine version was used; literary magazine editors made very few changes—if any—even printing Bukowski’s unintended typographical mistakes. The sources below indicate which version is being used for each poem as well as its date of publication. Poems flagged as uncollected have previously appeared in small press magazines only, but given their obscure nature and limited print runs—200 or 300 copies, if that—it is almost as if they were never actually published. Likewise, while some of the poems printed in this collection have appeared in previous Black Sparrow Press and Ecco volumes of poetry, the versions made available here have never been published before. This book, then, is a collection of new poetry and prose by Charles Bukowski. ∫ “All the eating places were closed . . .” Excerpt from “Aftermath of a Lengthy Rejection Slip,” Story, March–April 1944; collected in Portions from a Wine-Stained Notebook , 2008. “A cat walks by . . .” Excerpt from “poem for personnel managers,” Quixote 13, Spring 1957. “I don’t want to draw . . .” Excerpt from “bring down the beams,” Hearse 4, early 1959. “conversation on a telephone.” Targets 4, December 1960; collected in The Days Run Away Like Wild Horses Over the Hills , 1969. “I saw that bird and . . .” Excerpt from a July 24, 1960, letter to Sheri Martinelli; Beerspit Night and Cursing, 2001. “I saw a bird when . . .” Excerpt from a late July 1960 letter to Jory Sherman; Screams from the Balcony, 1993. “the cat.” c. 1960–61 manuscript; previously unpublished. “The Arabians admire the cat . . .” Excerpt from a December 21, 1960, letter to Sheri Martinelli; Beerspit Night and Cursing . “I do not always hate the cat that kills the bird, only the cat that kills me . . .” c. 1963 manuscript; previously unpublished. “Small birds who go . . .” This line was used as a subtitle for It Catches My Heart in Its Hands, 1963. “startled into life like fire.” Florida Education 42.4, December 1964, where it was published as “startled into steam of life like fire.” Collected in Burning in Water, Drowning in Flame , 1974. “I was born to hustle roses down the avenues of the dead.” Crucifix in a Deathhand, 1965. “The factories, the jails . . .” Excerpt from an early August 1965 letter to Jim Roman; previously unpublished. “the devious good of rescuing the suffering.” Spectroscope 1, April 1966; previously uncollected, based on a poem titled “cat” written on November 6, 1964. “portrait of a soul for flies.” Intermission, September 1966; previously uncollected. “sensible brush, sleeping . . .” Untitled poem published in Hiram Poetry Review 1, Fall–Winter 1966; collected as “the cat” in The Days . . . “I don’t like love as a command . . .” Excerpt from a November 18, 1966, letter to Carl Weissner; Screams from the Balcony . “the mockingbird.” April 1971 manuscript; collected in Mockingbird Wish Me Luck , 1972. “looking at the cat’s balls.” September 7, 1971, manuscript; previously uncollected. “the strangest thing.” Early to mid-1970s manuscript; collected in Play the Piano Drunk Like a Percussion Instrument Until the Fingers Begin to Bleed a Bit , 1979. “wet night.” Burning in Water, Drowning in Flame, 1974. “cats kill cats . . .” Excerpt from “the joke,” September 15, 1975, manuscript; collected as “the cosmic joke” in The Night Torn Mad with Footsteps, 2001. “little tigers everywhere.” November 14, 1975, manuscript; collected in Love Is a Dog from Hell , 1977. “love is the crushed cats . . .” Excerpt from “a definition,” November 14, 1975, manuscript; collected in The Night Torn . . . “I walked into the kitchen . . .” Excerpt from last chapter of Women, 1978. “bad fix.” June 13, 1978, manuscript; collected in Dangling in Tournefortia , 1981. “gift.” July 16, 1978, manuscript; previously uncollected. “Butch Van Gogh.” November 9, 1978, manuscript; collected in Open All Night , 2000. “a reader.” August 27, 1979, manuscript; previously unpublished. “Manx.” December 23, 1979, manuscript; collected in Open All Night . “An international thief . . .” Excerpt from a June 10, 1981, letter to Carl Weissner; previously unpublished. “The Manx is walking again . . .” Excerpt from a June 28, 1981, letter to Carl Weissner; previously unpublished. “Now here’s a beautiful cat . . .” Excerpt from “Charles Bukowski,” an interview with Penny Grenoble; South Bay , November 1981; previously uncollected. “the manx came to the door . . .” Excerpt from a January 27, 1982, letter to Louise Webb; Screams from the Balcony . “night work.” March 4, 1980, manuscript; collected in Dangling . . . “One day I was standing around . . .” Excerpt from Ham on Rye, 1982. “cats and people and you and me and everything.” September 14, 1981, manuscript; collected as “in other words” in Bone Palace Ballet, 1997, and as “cats and you and me” in The Night Torn . . . “I find my place, pull into . . .” Excerpt from a “Notes of a Dirty Old Man” column written in November 1982, posthumously published as “Death in the Afternoon” in Betting on the Muse, 1996. “the history of a tough motherfucker.” February 28, 1983, manuscript (second draft); collected in War All the Time , 1984. “The tailless, cross-eyed cat . . .” Short note published after reprint of “the history of a tough motherfucker” in Arete 2.1 , July/August 1989; previously uncollected. “terminology.” August 20, 1983, manuscript; collected in War All the Time . “one for the old boy.” August 1983 manuscript; collected in War All the Time . “a nature poem for you.” June 26, 1984, manuscript; collected as “an animal poem” in The Night Torn . . . “a sensible fellow.” October 1984 manuscript; previously uncollected. “wearing the collar.” March 1985 manuscript; collected in You Get So Alone at Times That It Just Makes Sense , 1986. “exactly fine.” November 15, 1985, manuscript; collected as “exactly right” in The Night Torn . . . “In the morning we awakened . . .” Excerpt from The Wedding, November 1985 manuscript; previously uncollected. “a cat is a cat is a cat is a cat.” Wormwood Review 128, 1992; previously published in You Get So Alone . . . “another casualty.” You Get So Alone . . . “my cat, the writer.” June 18, 1986, manuscript; collected in The Night Torn . . . “5 cats.” c. 1986 manuscript; previously unpublished. “Having a bunch of cats . . .” Excerpt from “Tough Guys Write Poetry,” an interview with Sean Penn; Interview, September 1987. “warm light.” Warm Light bookmark, September 1990; collected in The Last Night of the Earth Poems , 1992. “the dream.” January 16, 1990, manuscript; previously uncollected. “So you’ve got a talking cat . . .” Excerpt from a January 28, 1990, letter to William Packard; Reach for the Sun, 1999. “some of this place.” May 7, 1990, manuscript; collected as “this place” in Sifting Through the Madness for the Word, the Line, the Way, 2003. “our gang.” November 25, 1990, manuscript; previously uncollected. “unclassical symphony.” December 31, 1990, manuscript; collected in Sifting Through the Madness . . . “war surplus.” c. 1990 manuscript; collected as “military surplus” in Slouching Toward Nirvana, 2005. “when everything seems like suicide finality.” Raccoon 30/31, September 1991; previously uncollected. “I walked up the driveway . . .” Excerpt from an October 2, 1991, journal entry published in The Captain Is Out to Lunch and the Sailors Have Taken Over the Ship, 1998. “cool fur.” October 23, 1991, manuscript; collected in Bone Palace Ballet , 1997. “consummation.” c. early 1990s manuscript; collected in The Continual Condition , 2009. “tragedy?” New York Quarterly 49, 1992; collected as “reunion” in Bone Palace Ballet , and in The Continual Condition . “Do you have a cat? . . .” Excerpt from an April 16, 1992, journal entry published in The Captain Is Out . . . “We now have 9 cats . . .” Excerpt from an October 13, 1992, letter to Louise Webb; Reach for the Sun. “my cats.” c. 1989 manuscript; collected in Come on In , 2006.
